prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: I keep base editing as my preferred configuration, and the first round has not changed my view of its science. It is a new piece of chemistry in a living genome: a defined deamination of one nucleobase, directed by a guide, with no double-strand break. The adenine editor needed a deaminase evolved to act on DNA, which is the protein-engineering side of chemistry done properly. The consequences are visible in every genetics laboratory and in the first treated patients. It is also the only configuration on the table where attribution to three names is straightforward: Liu as the conceptual and experimental driver, Komor for the cytosine editor and Gaudelli for the adenine editor. The chair's question about whether reproducibility and clean attribution should outweigh conceptual reach is where I come out in favour of this candidate, because it has both a clear concept and a clean credit line, unlike most of the other candidates here.
statement.case_against: The reservations I gave in round 1 stand and nobody has answered them. Base editing is about ten years old, the clinical record is short, and bystander and off-target deamination are still being engineered away. It sits close to the 2020 prize on CRISPR-Cas9, and I cannot claim the committee will see it as separable. Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID work is a real priority question that a Liu, Komor, Gaudelli trio leaves open, and a citation that says nothing about it will be read as a decision. Prime editing (B038) is not on the shortlist, but it may eventually be judged the more general advance and could argue for a later, combined prize. With five ballots split two, two, two, one and one, I do not read my single vote as evidence that the committee should choose this one, and I would rather see it lose to a better-settled case than win by default.

responses.point: Chabes supports B068 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, with a citation confined to bifunctional PROTAC molecules, and concedes that this omits the cereblon and glue lineage that has the most patient benefit so far.
responses.response: Your citation wording partly meets the condition I set in round 1, because it is explicitly confined to PROTACs and does not claim the glue lineage. My difficulty is the one you state yourself: the part of the field with approved drugs sits outside the trio, and that makes the prize look as if it rewards the concept while ignoring the clinical evidence. Your own point about Handa or Sakamoto as a possible third name shows that the third place is not settled. Ciulli's contribution is the structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex rationalisation. That is real chemistry and fits my own taste, but it is refinement of a concept that Crews and Deshaies set out in 2001. I rate B068 close to B024 and I would move to it if the committee agrees to a PROTAC-only citation and to a deliberate choice between Ciulli and Handa for the third name. I have not moved yet, because that agreement is not in the record.

responses.point: Aili argues that B068 is the clearest chemical design principle on the shortlist, since an event-driven, catalytic degrader mode of action is a new pharmacological principle, and offers narrowing the citation to the PROTAC concept.
responses.response: I agree that event-driven, catalytic degradation is the best argument for B068 and that it is a mechanistic claim, not a phenotype. I also accept your offer to narrow the citation as the more honest route, and I would prefer it to a broad degrader citation that implies credit for the glue discoveries. Where I disagree is the argument that 'many clinical candidates exist'. Candidates are not validation, and I hold base editing to the same standard on its short clinical record. We should apply the same maturity bar to both candidates and not excuse one of them. Since you yourself list the lack of an approved PROTAC drug as the main reservation, I read your position as agreeing that B068 would be an early prize.

responses.point: Sparr (with Linke) supports B003 with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as a physical-chemical principle of intracellular organisation, resting on the 2009 P-granule work and Rosen's multivalent reconstitution.
responses.response: The chair asks whether the citation can stand on the physical-chemical principle without asserting that particular condensates are phase-separated in vivo. I think it can, and your wording does it better than Linke's, which says that cells are organised into membraneless compartments and so makes the in vivo claim. If the principle is demixing driven by multivalency, then Rosen's reconstituted systems are the most quantitative part of the credit among the three names, and I would accept Rosen over Pappu on that basis. My remaining discomfort is that Pappu and Mittag supplied the sequence grammar, and I do not know how a citation can claim a principle while leaving out the people who made it predictive. I keep B003 as my third choice, with a clear preference for your citation wording over the broader one.

responses.point: Linke, as chair and first-choice supporter of B003, argues for a concept with generative reach and a dated origin, and says B068 or B023 would be the safer prize if the field is judged too contested.
responses.response: I accept your account of the 2009 origin and I accept that the generative reach is large. You have said that B068 would be safer, and I draw the same conclusion about the ordering of safety: B003 carries the most scientific dispute, B068 a clinical-timing dispute, and B024 a priority and 2020-overlap dispute. I do not think the committee should take the least disputed option by default, because that would favour B004 or B009, which are mature but are not what I mean by a game-changer. On B023, I agree with you that the attribution is clean. I stay at my round-1 view that the overlap with the 1998 and 2013 computational prizes and the indirect effect on experiments weigh against it, and I would declare my link to Warshel if it were seriously considered.

responses.point: Brzezinski supports B009 with Rees, Dean and Seefeldt, argues that the structures and kinetics are confirmed over three decades, and discloses that his preference partly reflects his interest in biological energy conversion.
responses.response: I value the disclosure and I agree that the structural evidence is excellent. The weakness is the one you list, that the mechanism of N2 reduction at the cofactor is not settled, and a citation that claims mechanism would not be accurate. Your citation says the work reveals 'how the cofactor binds and reduces dinitrogen', and that overreaches; Zou's version has the same problem. A structure-and-cofactor citation would be sound, but then the prize is a structural prize and I would want to know what is the new chemical capability it provides. I also see that the third name is open between Dean and Einsle, and Ribbe's claim is not answered, so B009 has the same attribution problem as the other candidates and is not clearly better than B024 on that ground.

responses.point: Somfai supports a two-person B004 prize for Buchwald and Hartwig, arguing that C-N coupling has a different mechanistic bottleneck from C-C coupling and that thirty years of confirmation removes any maturity question.
responses.response: Your argument that reductive elimination from amido complexes is a different problem from the C-C couplings is persuasive on the chemistry, and I accept that the attribution is clean. Maturity is not in question. It is the extent to which this is a game-changer compared with the 2010 prize that I doubt, and I am not convinced that a committee that has just recognised cross-coupling will treat this as separate. The Kosugi precursor can be handled by wording the citation around general catalytic coupling of amines, which you propose. I would not oppose B004 on scientific grounds, but I think its closeness to 2010 will cost it support, and I would rank it behind B068 and B024.

uncertainties: Whether Kondo and Nishida's independent Target-AID work should displace Komor or Gaudelli, and whether the committee accepts a Liu-centred trio.
Whether the committee treats base editing as separable from the 2020 CRISPR prize, and whether prime editing (B038) should be considered together with it in a later year.
Whether B068 can be limited to PROTACs with Ciulli as third name, or whether the glue lineage must be credited, in which case I would lean away from it for 2026.
How much weight the short clinical record of base editing should carry, given that I press the same point against B068.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for the preferred B024 configuration, and I have no connection to the base editing, degrader, phase separation or nitrogenase candidates. My professional connection to Arieh Warshel (USC postdoc, EVB collaboration) is unchanged. It is relevant to computational method candidates such as B023 and B032, and I would declare it and not rely on it if either were put forward.
